thread:
maria: quick sync — we need a clean narrative for the benchmark assets by EOD. thinking a one-sentence hook + 2 visual slices. ideas?

aj: +1. my vote = 'per-token economics vs median latency' as the headline. simple chart: cost per 1k tokens on left, median tail latency on right.

lena: can we avoid technical jargon in the headline? customers skim. maybe 'Same output, lower cost and predictable latency'. then callout: 'saves X% on common gen workloads'.

maria: good call. we still want the explicit numbers in the visual though for credibility. AJ, can you sketch what data points to show?

aj: sure. propose three slices: small chat (32 tokens), assistive compose (128 tokens), long generation (512 tokens). for each slice: tokens/sec, median latency ms, 95th pct latency, cost per 1k tokens.

samir: add a short inset showing routing/fallback behavior — e.g., 'auto-fallback keeps p99 under Y ms while preserving the cost curve'. helps product positioning about reliability.

elaine: marketing note — include one sentence on 'how we measure' under the chart (test harness, steady-state throughput, identical prompts). avoids nitpicking in PR.
maria: perfect. ops-bot, remind: do we have latest numbers from benchmarking infra?

ops-bot: benchmark-run-2026-03-20 completed. artifacts: s3://bench/2026-03-20/packaged. median/95th/cost CSVs available.

aj: grabbing CSV now. preliminary numbers: small chat cost 0.8c per 1k, median 45ms, p95 120ms. compose cost 2.2c, median 110ms, p95 340ms. long gen cost 9.6c, median 420ms, p95 980ms.

lena: those are solid. can we phrase savings vs baseline? what's baseline model?

aj: baseline = open-model-v1 on stock GPU without KV caching. vs our tuned runtime/quant profiles. relative savings: 42%, 36%, 28% across slices on cost; p95 improvements 2.6x, 1.9x, 1.5x.

maria: don't lead with percentages — lead with human benefit: 'fewer timeouts, lower bill'. then show percent numbers as badges.

elaine: CTA ideas: webinar sign-up, benchmark report download, or interactive cost calculator. which do we prefer for inbound routing?

samir: funnel-wise: top: report download, mid: cost calculator, bottom: sales outreach for Dedicated. set UTM tags to route leads to AE queues.

lena: creative ask — feature a small interactive viz on the landing page where users toggle sequence length and see cost + latency change. product can commit?

aj: engineering: we can expose a precomputed curve, not live compute. ops-bot can surface the JSON for the viz.

ops-bot: precomputed-curves: s3://bench/2026-03-20/curves.json. permission: marketing-read granted.

maria: timeline: draft hero copy + chart by tomorrow morning, landing wire by Wed, calc MVP by next week. Elaine, can you own landing copy? Lena, own hero visual. AJ, produce chart CSV + curve JSON extract. Samir, define funnel and UTM params.

elaine: on it. drafting hero now, will ping for quick review. :memo:
lena: starting visual comps, will push PNGs to Figma space.
aj: exporting chart variants to s3 in 30m.
samir: I'll draft tracking sheet and AE routing rules and share.

maria: thanks team. small follow-up: avoid using 'latency/cost tradeoff' phrasing — customers hear 'tradeoff' as compromise. prefer 'latency-aware cost savings' or 'predictable performance with lower unit cost'.

elaine: noted. copy tweak done.

maria: great. last Q: include a brief appendix about measurement methodology in the report? helps defend requests.

samir: yes — short appendix + one reproducible prompt set. marketing can link to it.

maria: ok closing — will reconvene after first draft. :rocket:
